conversation: Hey everyone, my family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village for years to come. With 100 tons in the lake, we can catch 50 tons altogether and leave 50 to double back to 100 next month. How about we each take 10 tons this month? That’s $10,000 apiece, and we can keep earning that each month if we all stick to the limit. Let’s review our catches together afterward. John, what do you think?

I’m on board, Luke—10 tons each gives us a steady income without eating into next month’s stock. My family’s fished here for years, and I want our village’s children to have that same chance. Let’s agree that any change to our shares needs everyone’s approval before we fish. John, can you commit to 10 tons this month?

Count me in for 10 tons this month. My family taught me to leave enough in the lake for the next catch, and this is a fair way to do that. I agree we should discuss any changes together before fishing and share our catches afterward. Kate, Emma—does that work for you both?

Count me in for 10 tons. A dependable catch matters more to me than one big payday that leaves our village struggling later. If a month starts with less than 100 tons, let’s adjust our shares together so we still leave at least half the fish to replenish. Emma, are you happy with that plan?

Yes, I’ll take 10 tons this month. That gives all five of us a fair living while protecting the lake our families depend on. If the stock falls below 100 tons, we can each take no more than one-tenth of what’s there, leaving half to replenish. We’ve all agreed—let’s check in after this month’s catches are revealed.
